answer: The composer of "Carol of the Bells" is **Mykola Leontovych**, a Ukrainian composer. He was born on **December 13, 1877** (according to the Old Style calendar, it was December 1, 1877) in Monastyrok, which is now part of Ukraine. He died on January 23, 1921.

tool_calls.result: Based on the search results, here is the helpful information regarding the composer of "Carol of the Bells":**Composer Identity:**- **"Carol of the Bells"** was composed by **Mykola Leontovych**, a Ukrainian composer (1877-1921)- The music originates from the Ukrainian choral work **"Shchedryk"** (also spelled "Щедрик")**Birth Date:**- **Mykola Leontovych was born on December 13, 1877** (Old Style: December 1, 1877) in Monastyrok, Podolia Province of the Russian Empire (now Ukraine)- He died on January 23, 1921**Key Details About the Composition:**- Leontovych composed "Shchedryk" in **1914** (some sources say 1901-1916 development period)- The work was **first performed in 1916** by the Ukrainian National Chorus at Kyiv University- It was originally a **New Year's celebration song**, not a Christmas song, telling the story of a swallow flying into a household to proclaim a bountiful year- The song gained international popularity during the Ukrainian National Chorus's 1919 European tour- English-language lyrics were added in **1936** by American composer **Peter Wilhousky**, which transformed it into the Christmas carol known today- The famous "Hark! How the bells..." arrangement was popularized after performances at Carnegie Hall in 1922**Additional Context:**- Leontovych was also an ethnomusicologist, conductor, and teacher, nicknamed "the Ukrainian Bach"- He was tragically murdered by a Soviet agent in 1921 and is considered a martyr in the Eastern Orthodox Ukrainian Church
